item.title: Batch renaming files from an Excel or CSV list: three approaches that actually work
item.author: Author
item.description:
Batch renaming files from an Excel or CSV list

If you are cleaning up photos, scans, lecture videos or invoices, the situation is usually the same: you already have a table. Column A is the current filename, column B is what you want it to be, maybe column C is a capture date and D is a client code. The hard part is not inventing new names. It is turning that table into actual renames on disk.

item.title: Two small sites went live: an Old English dictionary and a batch renamer
item.author: Author
item.description:
Two small sites went live: an Old English dictionary and a batch renamer

I wanted to test one question: can one person, with no budget and no ads, get anywhere by taking a very narrow need all the way to the end?

Rather than argue about it, I built two things. They sit at opposite ends of the spectrum — one is pure content, one is a pure tool — which makes them a clean control group.

item.title: Building and Deploying a Web App on Cloudflare Pages with Next.js, Hono.js, Drizzle and shadcn/ui
item.author: Author
item.description:
Building and Deploying a Web App on Cloudflare Pages with Next.js, Hono.js, Drizzle and shadcn/ui

Lately I’ve been taking advantage of Cloudflare’s free offerings—both Workers and Pages. After tinkering with a few small projects and getting through the initial exploration phase, I’d like to share the process of quickly building a Web App deployed on Cloudflare Pages using these open-source libraries.

If you don’t want to read through the process, you can skip straight to the end. I’ve shared the project address; just fork my example project and you can use it right away.

item.title: Bulk Delete Keys in `Cloudflare KV`
item.author: Author
item.description:
Bulk Delete Keys in Cloudflare KV

Get the List of keys

Run this first

1

pnpm wrangler kv:key list --namespace-id=${namespaceID} > PURGE.json`

This gives you the complete list of keys; if you need a condition, just add: --prefix="prefix"

Bulk Delete

1

cat purge.json | jq -r '.[].name' | xargs -I {} pnpm wrangler kv:key delete --namespace-id=${namespaceID} {}

item.title: Migrating a Remix Project to Cloudflare
item.author: Author
item.description:
Migrating a Remix Project to Cloudflare

Recently I developed a project using remix. I hadn’t done full-stack development before; I’d used reactjs a bit but wasn’t very familiar with it, and I was using Nextjs, which felt very hard to use — mainly because after version 13 switched to the app router, I was somewhat at a loss.

Later I discovered remix, which uses filename-based routing directly and is much more convenient, and the loader and action approach is also very intuitive, so I chose remix.

item.title: Migrating My Home Server from a Dell R720 to a Snail Interstellar + MacBook Pro: Follow-up
item.author: Author
item.description:
Migrating My Home Server from a Dell R720 to a Snail Interstellar + MacBook Pro: Follow-up

Gigabit Network Disconnection Problem

The migration is complete and I’ve been using it for a while. The Snail Interstellar’s power consumption is very low (compared with the R720’s 100+ watts); with 3 HDDs and 1 SSD it draws 35 watts, less than 1 kWh a day—very nice.

But there’s currently a problem: on the MacbookPro, as soon as I close the lid, lock the screen, or close the remote desktop, the wired network adapter on the Thunderbolt HUB disconnects.

item.title: A Problem Caused by a YouTube App Using QUIC
item.author: Author
item.description:
A Problem Caused by a YouTube App Using QUIC

Problem Description

At home, an r2s serves as the bypass router using sing-box in tun mode. I had always used a cn2 gia line, and every night I’d watch videos on youtube on my apple tv before going to sleep, with no problems. This month the server’s traffic ran out, so I switched to hysteria2 on an ordinary line. It was fine all day, but come evening youtube was completely unwatchable. I figured udp packet loss was probably severe in the evening, so I didn’t bother with it.

item.title: Migrating My Home Server from a Dell R720 to a Snail Interstellar + MacBook Pro
item.author: Author
item.description:
Migrating My Home Server from a Dell R720 to a Snail Interstellar + MacBook Pro

A few years ago I got into HomeLab and bought a second-hand Dell R720 rack server to use as a home server. But this server’s power consumption was too high—dual cpus idled at nearly 200w. After switching to low-power Xeons and installing only one cpu, it was still 100w+. Over a year the electricity bill added up, and in summer it got very hot. Later I used the ipmi tool and wrote some code in python to adjust the loud fans based on temperature, which made it much more comfortable, but in summer as the room temperature rose the fans still ramped up their speed dramatically. I always wanted to switch to a low-power server. I’d previously bought a Snail Interstellar, which uses a j1900 and has very low power consumption, so I migrated the home server from the Dell R720 to the Snail Interstellar.
